newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish minister probed over unlicenced pistol.
newsitem.headline: Polish minister probed over unlicenced pistol.

text.p: Poland's Interior Minister Leszek Miller, backer of a controversial bid to ease gun controls, faced investigation by prosecutors on Thursday after admitting he had owned a pistol for two years without a permit.

The Warsaw prosecutors' spokesman told PAP news agency a probe had been launched after Miller said on a television chat show he had been given a handgun in 1995 by a cabinet colleague and had never obtained a licence.
"Provincial prosecutors in Warsaw began...investigation of illegal possession of a firearm by Interior and Administration Ministry chief Leszek Miller," Ryszard Kucinski said.
Miller, who is in charge of Poland's police, has said he is willing to face the consequences of his oversight but argues it was not serious as he had kept the small gun in his safe.

The ex-communist minister backs a bill, soon to go before parliament, revising and clarifying Poland's gun laws. The bill is seen by supporters as a democratic move to give citizens freer access to arms for self-defence.

Some commentators say it will in effect oblige police to issue gun permits to applicants meeting certain criteria -- such as being over 21, healthy, resident in Poland, free of addictions, not suspected or convicted of violent crimes and not likely to use arms to commit an offense.

But police spokesman Andrzej Przemyski disputed this view and told Reuters applicants would still have to show they really needed and knew how to use a gun for self-defence, and the police would retain wide discretion in granting permits.
The bill has aroused strong controversy in Poland which has seen a surge in violent crime since the 1989 fall of communism. Opponents fear wider gun ownership could fuel armed crime.
